criteria.note: THE MECHANISM WORKS; THE PROOF AND THE UNIVERSAL DO NOT. The derivation itself is sound and I watched it run: my gate at 84e9233 reached the always-run stage and printed '156 verdict artifact(s) tracked, 156 already recorded, 0 derivable but not appended, 1 duplicate key(s) already in the log'. Two things fail the criterion anyway. FIRST, the assertion that carries AC1's completeness claim is pinned to a moving repository property, and its own text is the thing it falsifies: scripts/selftest.py:21163 closes with `str(len(_v22_domain)) not in _v22_events_src` under a sentence promising 'the corpus size appears NOWHERE as a literal in the module ... no assertion here is pinned to today's count'. I built the cleanest negative control I could (41 verdict artifacts added inside EXISTING proof directories, so no new spec ids and no index churn), committed, corpus 197, and ran the shipped suite: exit 1, 3230 passed 1 failed, and the SOLE failure is this AC1 domain assertion. Nearest false red is 41 artifacts away and round 3's own fix commit moved it there from 53. The item's own spec Notes line 287 says 'Do not pin any assertion to today's 154 verdicts or 596 events. Both grow. Derive.' SECOND, AC1's universal ('every verdict artifact in the repository has a corresponding verdict.recorded event' after a gate run) is defeasible with no mechanical resistance. In my own fixture one hand-emitted verdict.recorded carrying a crafted verdict_path made the reconciler withhold BOTH of that spec's appends on runs 1, 2 and 3, permanently, and validate.py accepted the resulting log at exit 0; the only thing forbidding the call is a docstring sentence. A tracked symlink at a verdict path (lane 2, refuter-confirmed) passes the contract stage GREEN while its event records no verdict, no round and no commit. The spec's own NO UNBACKED UNIVERSAL note applies to its own headline claim.

MET, and the round-3 amendment is the reason it is now honestly met rather than refuted by its own evidence. Idempotence holds on the real corpus: my gate run reported 156 tracked and 156 already recorded with zero appended. The collapse and dedup behaviour was reproduced independently in three lanes and by two refuters: the shipped module appends [2,0,0,0] over a reformatted twin and [1,0,0] over byte-identical twins, 12 concurrent reconciliations produce 20 events with 20 distinct keys and 0 duplicates, and four repeated runs over a hand-seeded pre-fix residue append zero. The one duplicate key is round-1 path-key residue proven by provenance (both events carry no verdict_blob), it is REPORTED on every run (I saw it in my own gate line), and the permanent reader-side over-count is declared and assigned to the metrics split. The narrowing of 'a duplicate key in the log' to 'a duplicate key APPENDED BY A RECONCILIATION' is legitimate rather than unfalsifiable: a lane falsified the new clause against the pre-fix module 528c98f (run 1 appended two events for one key) and could not falsify it against the shipped one. Teeth gaps survive around this criterion (the batch route's equivalence assertion becomes a comparison of the fallback with itself when the batch fails; the ragged-answer guard is untested), but the correctness dimension AC2 actually claims does have teeth, and no wrong key can be appended: everything appended comes from verdict_domain, whose keys are read from the git index.

MET. Verified in part by me and in part by named lanes. I confirmed the instruction is gone in substance: the item's whole thesis rests on it and the review skill no longer carries either invented name. Lanes 5 and 7 independently ran `git grep -l` for review.passed and review.failed over the tracked corpus and got exactly TEN files, equal in both directions to the _V22_RECORDS enumeration in scripts/selftest.py, with the round-2 error ('NOW ELEVEN ENTRIES') confirmed as genuinely corrected this round; the fifteen live engine surfaces (seven review SKILL.md copies, eight capabilities.yaml) carry neither name; and neither name is in EVENT_TYPES in either validate.py or events.py, which is the sharper half of the lesson the criterion records. I did not personally re-run the ten-file enumeration and am attributing it. The round-2 amendment from 'an EMPTY LIST' to an equality against an enumerated list with reasons was already ruled legitimate and I see no reason to disturb that: a shipped proof manifest cannot be edited without moving the proof_digest its own verdict carries, which is a measured impossibility rather than a reinterpretation after the fact. NOTE THAT DOES NOT CHANGE THE RULING: this criterion is the one that establishes prose instructions get DELETED rather than corrected, and the same commit that satisfies it adds a prose prohibition with no code guard (must-fix 3). That is charged against AC1's universal, not against AC3's letter, which is satisfied.

disposition: DO NOT LAND. Round 4 is warranted and three things stand between here and landing. All three live in files already inside this item's declared footprint, none needs a new protected-path approval, and all three belong in ONE commit. (1) Replace the substring test at scripts/selftest.py:21163 with a mechanism that is not pinned to the corpus size: a digit-bounded scan over code rather than over docstrings, or an expectation derived from the owner's constants. Then ask the WARP-1210 question out loud in the manifest: what ordinary future change breaks this assertion? The literals `154` and `1970 and 2099` that round 3 wrote into the module docstring are what shortened the fuse from 53 artifacts to 41, so either they go or the mechanism does. (2) Correct or delete the manifest's 'a154a and a--diff-filtera appear ZERO times in all eight copies of the module', re-measured at whatever commit actually ships. Do not bump it; measure it. (3) Refuse VERDICT_EVENT in emit() and main() unless the producer is the reconciler, add the assertion that proves the refusal, and make the integrity line NAME the unresolvable event instead of counting it, mirroring what the deferred branch already does one line above. RIDE ALONG IN THE SAME COMMIT, because the round is open and each is one or two lines: tighten _iso_z to mean the one format the envelope writes (a regex, or a strftime round-trip) and give the selftest's partition predicate an oracle that is not the module's own function; delete the false parenthetical 'the artifact declares no reviewed_at' and leave the bare count; turn the two new `[]` reads at selftest.py:21236 and :21423 into `.get`; add one report field naming which route resolved the legacy events, asserted to be the batch here; filter verdict_blob_map on index mode 100644 and 100755; delete the tautological clause at selftest.py:21448; correct the 'NUL so a path holding any byte is safe' docstring sentence, since it is the length guard and not the NUL that makes it safe; and make ONE structural pass over the spec and manifest that DELETES every absolute corpus figure or anchors it to a named revision. Never bump a corpus count in this item again: the round's own verdict artifact is what invalidates it, so bumping reproduces the error a fourth time. DO NOT gate landing on the red `generated` stage: I measured it red at origin/main a8b81b9 too, the date stamp dates from 0de75f3 (WARP-0100), and the ship ritual regenerates specs/index.md anyway. It needs its own item, not this one.

headline: FAIL, on a real and reproduced defect rather than on prose. Round 3 fixed what round 2 broke and its two spec amendments are both legitimate narrowings that made criteria true rather than unfalsifiable, but the assertion that carries AC1's completeness claim is itself pinned to a moving repository property, and it is the one assertion whose published text promises it is not. scripts/selftest.py:21163 closes with `str(len(_v22_domain)) not in _v22_events_src`, a substring test of the tracked verdict corpus size against the whole text of .warp/events.py. I built the cleanest negative control available (41 verdict artifacts inside existing proof directories, no new spec ids, no index churn), took the corpus to 197, and ran the shipped suite: exit 1, 3230 passed 1 failed, and the SOLE failure is that assertion, on a stage verify.sh:19 declares `required`. The nearest false red is 41 artifacts away, this repository grew 150 to 156 in two days, and round 3's own fix commit shortened the fuse from 53 to 41 by writing `1970 and 2099` into the module docstring. This is verbatim the WARP-1210 `== 139` law, and it breaks the item's OWN written rule (spec Notes line 287: 'Do not pin any assertion to today's 154 verdicts or 596 events. Both grow. Derive.'). Two further blocking items compound it: the manifest certifies that `154` appears ZERO times in all eight copies of the module when it appears once in every one, at line 350, put there by the very commit the manifest binds to, and that false sentence is precisely the premise that hid the first defect from three rounds of review; and AC1's universal is defeasible with no mechanical resistance, since one hand-emitted verdict.recorded permanently withholds a whole spec's projection (I reproduced it: emit exits 0, three runs each withhold, validate.py accepts the log at exit 0) against nothing but a docstring sentence, in the one item whose entire thesis is that if it matters it is code and not prose. Everything else the seven lanes surfaced is non-blocking and rides along: eighteen further findings survived refutation, none of them worth a round on its own, and six were correctly refuted. The gate is RED at HEAD today, but I measured that red at origin/main too and it is a calendar-date artifact of check_generated, not this item's.

The corpus size is the count of tracked proof/*/verdict*.json, which every review round increments. scripts/verify.sh:19 declares CHECK_unit="required:python3 scripts/selftest.py", so a failure here is a red required gate. My own sweep of every integer whose decimal form occurs as a substring of the shipped module gives, above the current 156: 197, 208, 209, 234, 256, 345, 456, 567, 619, 678, 711, 722 and more. At the round-2 module the nearest collision above the corpus was 208, so this round shortened the fuse from 53 artifacts to 41. The clause is this item's OWN: 0 occurrences at a8b81b9, 1 at 04552de. Three aggravators. The assertion's own published text reads 'the corpus size appears NOWHERE as a literal in the module, so the domain grows with the repository and no assertion here is pinned to today's count', so the assertion states the negation of its own defect. The item's spec Notes line 287 reads 'Do not pin any assertion to today's 154 verdicts or 596 events. Both grow. Derive.' must_fix_before_live.why_blocking: In roughly 41 more tracked verdict artifacts the required gate goes RED for whatever unrelated item is in flight, with a failure message that blames the WARP-0722 domain enumeration while the actual cause is somebody having committed one more review. I measured the growth: 150 artifacts on 2026-07-26 and 156 on 2026-07-27, and WARP-1210 alone produced 14 verdict artifacts across its rounds, so this is scheduled rather than hypothetical. My brief is explicit that a hardcoded count pinned to a moving repository property is blocking even when the gate is green today, and the project's own recorded law is absolute. Two refuters independently confirmed the mechanism and one upgraded it to blocking on evidence the reporting lane had not gathered. Two corrections that narrow the blast radius but do not save it: no pack or plugin template ships a selftest (all seven pack copies of verify.sh carry CHECK_unit=""), so the damage is confined to the WARP home repository, and the red is transient because it fires only when the count EQUALS a colliding value. Confined and transient still means a red required gate on an innocent item, whose only workaround would be to commit another verdict file.

Either scan for a DIGIT-BOUNDED literal over CODE rather than over the whole file including docstrings, or derive the expectation from the owner's own constants instead of from the corpus size, so the assertion cannot be falsified by the repository growing. Then remove the `154` and the `1970 and 2099` literals that round 3 wrote into the module docstring, or accept that they belong there and change the mechanism to tolerate them. Whichever way it goes, record in the manifest the answer to the WARP-1210 question the law demands: what ordinary future change breaks this assertion? I tested three readings that might rescue it and none does: the token is a bare decimal, not a backticked one (the backticks on that line surround `git rev-parse`); 'all eight copies of the module' is the manifest's own phrase for exactly the eight events.py copies it enumerates elsewhere; and grep -n shows the token standing alone between spaces rather than inside a longer digit run.
must_fix_before_live.why_blocking: This is not a cosmetic count. It is the AC1 certification about the one file the item is named after, it is false in eight shipped files, and it is the specific sentence a reviewer reads to conclude that no bare corpus count lives in the module. That conclusion is exactly the premise that made MF1 invisible for three rounds and seven lanes: if the module holds no bare count, nobody asks what happens when the corpus size equals a digit run inside it. It now does, at 197. The manifest also carries a check, assertion_integrity, whose stated purpose is to catch this class ('THE ONE FIGURE ROUND 2 CARRIED FORWARD WITHOUT REMEASURING IS THE CLASS THIS CHECK EXISTS TO CATCH'), so the round that documents the pattern reproduced it. Both prior rounds were failed partly on published figures that had gone stale; a false zero-count in the evidence for the failing criterion is load-bearing in a way the merely off-by-one corpus figures elsewhere are not.

That is a prose rule with no mechanical check. verdict.recorded is still in EVENT_TYPES, emit() and the emit subcommand still accept it, the CLI exits 0, and the field flag lets a caller attach a verdict_path. logged_verdict_state derives the blocked spec id from that verdict_path, so one such line permanently withholds EVERY append for that spec id, on every run, in a log the module itself says nothing may rewrite. The module says the damage 'is reported by name ... which is how you would find out', and AC2 says such an event is 'NAMED and skipped', but _report_line interpolates only two integers for unresolved_legacy while the deferred branch one line above it joins the actual paths. The names exist only in the json report, which verify.sh does not request. So you learn that one event is poisoning a projection and not which one. One correction to the reporting lane: the invocation the eight copies advertised until 63c3742 does NOT produce the withholding (run verbatim it appends normally), so the trigger needs a crafted verdict_path plus an unresolvable commit. Round 3 improved this by deleting that worked example; it did not close it.
must_fix_before_live.why_blocking: AC1 claims that after a gate run every verdict artifact in the repository has a corresponding event. And the item's own thesis, its AC3, and the manifest's own prose_narrowed check all say that unenforced prose goes wrong, in the same commit that adds an unenforced prose prohibition to the module. That is the self-contradiction class round 2 was failed for, one layer down. Under the rule that a mechanism which can silently fail is a defect and not a note, and given the fix is two lines in files already inside this item's footprint while the round is already being reopened for MF1, this gets closed now rather than deferred. notes: FINDING COUNT IS NOT FINDING COUNT. Twenty-eight findings survived refutation, but they are not twenty-eight issues. Deduplicated: the pinned substring assertion is one defect found twice (lanes 5 and 6); the stage line's false parenthetical is one string literal found three times (lanes 1, 2 and 4) and classed differently each time; the stale corpus figures are one class found five times (lanes 3, 5, 6 and 7); the rule_1 residual miscount twice (lanes 5 and 7); the batch-never-runs teeth gap twice (lanes 2 and 6); the clock tautology twice (lanes 2 and 6). The real inventory is three blocking items and roughly ten distinct non-blocking ones. I have ruled once per issue rather than once per report, and the ride-along list in the disposition is the deduplicated set.

THE STAGE LINE'S PARENTHETICAL IS A RECORD ERROR, NOT WORDING, AND I OVERRULE THE LANE THAT SAID OTHERWISE. .warp/events.py:582 to 584 prints '%d dated at reconciliation (the artifact declares no reviewed_at)' for every event in that bucket, including artifacts that DO declare a reviewed_at in a legal ISO form the envelope refuses. Lane 1's refuter downgraded it to wording on the grounds that the remedy is an eight-word parenthetical. I disagree on the class while agreeing on the severity: the sentence is not arguable or a matter of phrasing, it is FALSE about the artifact it reports on, and the module's own section header at :164 to :167 explicitly separates the two causes the line collapses, so the collapsed reading is not supported by the module's own language. It never prints in warp today (all 156 tracked verdicts carry a Z-form reviewed_at, which is why my gate line shows no such clause), but datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() emits an offset, so an adopter writing the field the obvious way hits it immediately, and the item's own round-3 fixture WARP-9761 is built on exactly that shape while asserting only the counter and never the string. Remedy is deletion of the parenthetical, leaving the bare count.

_iso_z DOES NOT MEAN WHAT ITS DOCSTRING SAYS, AND THE PROOF SHARES THE PREDICATE. CPython compiles strptime formats case-insensitively with single-or-double-digit field regexes, so lowercase t and z forms pass the 'ONE format this envelope writes' predicate and land verbatim in the append-only log, while the selftest's own partition predicate at scripts/selftest.py:21212 to :21216 IS EV22._iso_z. So the amended AC1's format half cannot disagree with whatever the module happens to accept. A refuter measured that no published metric actually moves and corrected the reporting lane's overstated downstream harm, and the corpus is 156 of 156 strictly canonical, which is why this is non-blocking. It is still a real defect with a one-line fix, and fixing it makes the module, spec and manifest sentences true instead of requiring their deletion.

TWO NEW RAISE SITES IN THE COMMIT THAT DECLARED THE PRINCIPLE. spec_edit_ruling: TWO AMENDMENTS THIS ROUND, AND BOTH MADE THEIR CRITERION TRUE RATHER THAN UNFALSIFIABLE. I attacked each as a suspected retreat before accepting it. AMENDMENT 1, AC1's timestamp partition. Round 2 asserted the event's timestamp EQUALS the artifact's reviewed_at for every artifact, which flatly contradicted the module's own declared reconciliation fallback; committing one valid artifact shaped like the SHIPPED verdict example turned the gate red and made the declared fallback unreachable, so both halves could not hold. Round 3 replaced the universal with two branches that are TOTAL over the same domain, and crucially required BOTH to be exercised by fixtures rather than forbidding one. That is the legitimate move: the domain did not shrink, the verdict, round and reviewed-commit assertions stayed unconditional, and the criterion retains a reachable refutation. It is still falsifiable and lanes falsified mutants against it. ONE RESERVATION THAT DOES NOT INVALIDATE THE AMENDMENT: the partition's routing predicate is the module's own _iso_z, and the selftest's partition helper calls that same function, so the 'ONE format this envelope writes' half of the amended criterion has no oracle independent of the code it judges, and a widened _iso_z survives the whole suite. The amendment is sound; its proof is circular, and that is a non-blocking defect to close with a literal strptime on the test side. AMENDMENT 2, AC2's 'a duplicate key in the log' becoming 'a duplicate key APPENDED BY A RECONCILIATION'. This is the one that looks like a weakening and is not. The old clause was refuted by the item's own evidence while the criterion was marked passed, because the shipped log holds one duplicate that no code change can withdraw from an append-only file. The narrowing moves the clause to what the code actually controls, and it is not vacuous: a lane falsified the NEW clause against the pre-fix module 528c98f, where run 1 appended two events for one key, and could not falsify it against the shipped one. So the narrowing is exactly the clause that then caught a real defect three prior reviews had missed. The excluded residue is not swept away either: its provenance is proven (both events carry no verdict_blob, so both predate the content key), the DECLARED paragraph names it, it is reported on every run, and the permanent reader-side over-count is assigned to the metrics split. Legitimate. ONE FIGURE INSIDE THE SPEC IS NOT LEGITIMATE, AND IT IS NOT AN AMENDMENT BUT A SILENT RE-MEASUREMENT. The clause labelled 'AMENDED IN ROUND 2' reads 'the 155 artifacts yield 155 distinct reviews', and git log -L shows the round-3 FIX commit changed that very line from 154 to 155 while leaving the round-2 label in place, after which the round-3 EVIDENCE commit made it 156. A live number wearing a historical label is how this figure has now gone stale three rounds running. The substance still holds, so it is non-blocking, but the remedy is deletion or an explicit revision anchor, never a fourth bump: the round's own verdict artifact is the thing that falsifies it.
